allocations.description: Allocate one timer of TIM1, TIM2, TIM8, TIM12 or TIM15 and a pad one of its channels is routed to, for PWM, output compare or input capture written by the application. Allocation only: no code is generated and the timer is not shared.
allocations.guidance: Allocation only; no component is generated. resource_bindings gives the timer's hal_instance and clock_enable_api, the pad's port_symbol, pin_symbol and clock_enable_api, and under routes the selected signal with its alternate_symbol and channel_symbol. The application enables the TIM module if no other selected card does (USE_HAL_TIM_MODULE in generated/hal/stm32c5xx_hal_conf.h and stm32c5xx_drivers/hal/stm32c5xx_hal_tim.c in CMakeLists.txt), enables both clocks, initializes the pad with mode HAL_GPIO_MODE_ALTERNATE and the route's alternate_symbol, and drives the channel through the SDK TIM API in stm32c5xx_hal_tim.h starting from HAL_TIM_Init with the allocated hal_instance. Period, duty, polarity, compare or capture mode, complementary outputs, dead time and break are application decisions. One counter serves all channels, so the allocation takes the whole timer. No timing, electrical or errata qualification.

allocations.description: Allocate a pad routed to an external input of ADC1 for analog conversion written by the application. Allocation only: no code is generated; the converter is shared, one allocation per offered input. Pads that need the SBS pin remap are not offered.
allocations.guidance: Allocation only; no component is generated. resource_bindings gives the converter's hal_instance and clock_enable_api, the pad's port_symbol, pin_symbol and clock_enable_api, and under routes the selected signal with its channel_symbol. The application enables the ADC module (USE_HAL_ADC_MODULE in generated/hal/stm32c5xx_hal_conf.h and stm32c5xx_drivers/hal/stm32c5xx_hal_adc.c in CMakeLists.txt), enables both clocks, initializes the pad with mode HAL_GPIO_MODE_ANALOG, and configures and reads the converter through the SDK ADC API in stm32c5xx_hal_adc.h starting from HAL_ADC_Init with the allocated hal_instance. The converter is one shared unit: sequencing of several inputs, sampling time, calibration, reference voltage and accuracy are application decisions. Internal channels, injected and differential conversion are not covered. Only the pad each input uses at reset is offered: PC4, PC5, PB0 and PB1 need the SBS pin remap and are excluded, so no remap is required. No electrical or errata qualification.

allocations.description: One edge-aligned PWM output on a covered channel timer and a pad one of its channels is routed to. The frequency is one of the exact divisions of the pinned 144MHz timer clock; duty is set at run time in thousandths of the period. Generated component with init, start, set duty and stop. The whole timer belongs to the output.
allocations.guidance: Generated component owns the timer handle, the time base, one compare unit in PWM mode 1 with preload, the channel and the pad. Use the returned interface; do not initialize the timer, the channel or the pad again. Supports only the listed frequencies at the captured 144MHz kernel clock: each has an exact prescaler and period, the period is at least 1000 counts and full duty fits a 16-bit compare register. Duty is thousandths of the period rounded down to a whole count; the duty in force from a period boundary on is the last one written before it. The first period after a start can be shorter at the pad, never longer. start and stop belong to one thread; set duty may also run in an interrupt. Active high, counting up, internal clock; no dithering, complementary output, dead time, break input, one-pulse or any other channel of the timer. On a timer with a break function the SDK sets the main output enable when the channel starts. The level of the pad while stopped is not established. Init verifies the clock and register factors; dynamic clock changes are outside the contract. Build is not a measurement of frequency, duty or edge quality.

cites.statement: BKPT exact PWM frequency domain derived from the pinned 144MHz profile: prescaler and period for each choice, period between 999 and 65534. Arithmetic on the nominal clock, not measured timing.

interface.setup: Already initialized after mx_system_init. Header bkpt_components/{{unit}}.h; private timer handle, time base, compare unit, channel and pad. No manual timer, channel or GPIO setup.
interface.start: {{unit}}_start(duty_permille), 0..1000: checked HAL_OK restarts the counter and then enables the nominal {{frequency_hz}}Hz output, so the first period at the pad can be shorter than a full one and every later period is whole. One thread only, never from an interrupt; fails while running.
interface.set_duty: {{unit}}_set_duty(duty_permille), 0..1000, rounded down to a whole count of the {{period}}+1 count period: checked HAL_OK; the duty in force from a period boundary on is the last one written before it. Fails unless running. Owning thread or an interrupt; an interrupt that preempts start or stop gets a failure until start has finished and from the moment stop begins.
interface.stop: {{unit}}_stop(): checked HAL_OK stops the output, then the counter; idempotent when stopped. One thread only, never from an interrupt.
interface.scope: Exact factors and run-time clock/register checks for the pinned 144MHz profile. Active high, edge aligned. No clock changes, complementary outputs, dead time, break inputs, other channels, DMA or measured timing. The pad level while stopped is not established.

allocations.description: Read one analog input of a covered converter on request: a generated unit per input with init and a blocking read that returns the 12-bit count, the pad voltage as a fraction of VREF+. The converter is shared, so every offered input may have one unit. Pads that need the SBS pin remap are not offered.
allocations.guidance: Generated component. The first unit on a converter sets the ADC and DAC kernel clock to HCLK divided by 8 (18MHz in the captured 144MHz profile), 12-bit resolution, software trigger and one conversion per request, activates the converter and runs its offset calibration; every unit on that converter shares the one handle, and each unit switches its own pad to analog mode. Use the returned interface; do not initialize the converter, its clock or the pad again. read converts once with the longest sampling time and returns counts 0..4095, right aligned: a fraction of VREF+, not volts, because the reference is not measured. A read of another input than the previous one stops, switches, starts and calibrates the converter first. One thread only, never from an interrupt. The same kernel clock feeds the DAC. No internal channels, injected or differential conversion, triggers, interrupts, DMA, oversampling or analog watchdog. PC4, PC5, PB0 and PB1 need the SBS pin remap and are excluded. Accuracy, source impedance and noise are not qualified; build is not a measurement.

cites.statement: DS15135 page 76, ADC characteristics: the ADC clock frequency fADC is 8 to 36 MHz for a VDDA of 2.7 to 3.6 V. Text extraction of a table; the row is quoted, the table layout is not visually validated.
SDK build adds hal_adc.c only under its HAL ADC component selection; the captured build selects no such component, so the file is added through the root extension point.

interface.setup: Already initialized after mx_system_init. Header bkpt_components/{{unit}}.h; the converter, its kernel clock, calibration and the pad {{pad_name}} are set up. No manual ADC, clock or GPIO setup.
interface.read: {{unit}}_read(&counts): checked HAL_OK converts this input once, blocking for at most a few milliseconds, and writes counts 0..4095, the pad voltage as a fraction of VREF+ in steps of 1/4096. Not volts: the reference is not measured. One thread only, never from an interrupt, never while another unit of the same converter reads.
interface.scope: 12-bit, software trigger, longest sampling time, 18MHz converter clock checked at init for the pinned 144MHz profile. A read after a read of another input restarts and recalibrates the converter first. No internal channels, triggers, interrupts, DMA, oversampling or measured accuracy.

allocations.description: Measure the period and high time of a digital signal on a pad one channel of a covered timer is routed to: a generated unit with init and a blocking, polled measurement in microseconds with a time limit. The whole timer belongs to the measurement.
allocations.guidance: Generated component owns the timer handle, a 1MHz time base over a 16-bit period, capture of both edges on the allocated channel's own pin, and the pad as an input with the selected pull. Use the returned interface; do not initialize the timer, the channel or the pad again. measure waits for a rising edge, the falling edge after it and the next rising edge and returns period and high time in whole microseconds of the timer clock, or HAL_TIMEOUT after the time limit the caller passes, 1..60000 ms. The capture register is polled: edges closer together than the loop can follow are reported as HAL_ERROR through the overcapture flag or a capture found waiting, never as a wrong value, and the same happens when an interrupt holds the thread across two edges. One thread only, never from an interrupt. No input filter, prescaled capture, interrupt or DMA capture, other channels or XOR input. Init verifies the clock and register factors for the pinned 144MHz profile; times are counts of the nominal clock, not measured against a reference.

interface.setup: Already initialized after mx_system_init. Header bkpt_components/{{unit}}.h; private timer handle, 1MHz time base, capture of both edges and the pad {{pad_name}} as an input with pull {{pull}}. No manual timer, channel or GPIO setup.
interface.measure: {{unit}}_measure(timeout_ms, &period_us, &high_us), timeout 1..60000: checked HAL_OK waited for a rising edge, the falling edge after it and the next rising edge and wrote period and high time in microseconds. HAL_TIMEOUT when the edges did not arrive in time; HAL_ERROR when edges came faster than the polled capture could follow. Blocking; one thread only, never from an interrupt.
interface.scope: Polled capture with a microsecond count for the pinned 144MHz profile, checked at init and before each measurement. No stated minimum pulse width, input filter, interrupt or DMA capture or measured accuracy. Outputs are written only with HAL_OK.

guidance: All raw and managed UART profiles reference this shared card; absence means no UART initialization.

The fixed UART profiles reference this shared card. The managed UART transfer profile initializes a private handle of its own and does not use it. Absence means the captured handle is not initialized.

optional: USART2 and PA2/PA3 initialize only with the shared UART integration card.
Fixed UART profiles initialize the captured USART2 handle and PA2/PA3 via the shared UART card; the managed UART profile initializes its own private handle.

cite.statement: Authored managed UART unit declares its own static handle and initializes that handle for the allocated instance. BKPT-authored template, not manufacturer evidence.

assumption_replacements: GPIO interrupt composition covers PA4/PA5 CPU delivery only, with exclusive physical EXTI4/5 ownership across any consumers. Pending edge flags can coalesce. No complete EXTI/errata/electrical, shared-line or DMA-trigger coverage.

GPIO interrupt composition covers CPU delivery only, with exclusive ownership of each physical external line across any consumers. Pending edge flags can coalesce. No complete EXTI/errata/electrical, shared-line or DMA-trigger coverage.

instance_capabilities.description: Periodic update interrupt on a timer the timer channel allocation covers, with the generated component, exact rate choices and rules of periodic_interrupt on TIM6 and TIM7, unchanged. It takes the whole timer and its update vector and uses no channel or pad; use it when the basic timers are taken or more periodic interrupts are needed.
instance_capabilities.guidance: The reviewed periodic update component on a channel timer. Generated component owns persistent timer state, callback adapter, initialization, clock/factor verification, fresh-period start/stop and vector dispatch. Use returned interface; do not duplicate timer setup or weak callbacks. Supports only the complete declared set of exact nominal integer rates1..1000 at the captured144MHz kernel. PSC<=65534 and ARR1..65535; repetition0, upcounter/internal clock, no dithering. Init and start verify actual clock/register factors. Any dynamic clock changes are outside contract. Per-instance callback runs in IRQ context and must remain bounded; main/thread owns start/stop. Application chooses tick meaning. Build is not hardware rate/latency verification. The update vector is the timer's own update vector or, on a timer with one vector, its global vector; only the update event is enabled, and no channel of the timer is used.

pad_capabilities.description: Allocate a digital input on any pad eligible for general allocation. No code is generated: the application initializes the pad as an input with the pull it needs and reads it through the SDK.
pad_capabilities.guidance: Selected GPIO input after mx_system_init: use resource port_symbol, pin_symbol and clock_enable_api (zero arguments; void). Enable the selected clock, zero hal_gpio_config_t, set mode=HAL_GPIO_MODE_INPUT and pull=HAL_GPIO_PULL_NO, HAL_GPIO_PULL_UP or HAL_GPIO_PULL_DOWN, and check the HAL_GPIO_Init status. Read with HAL_GPIO_ReadPin(port_symbol, pin_symbol), which returns HAL_GPIO_PIN_SET or HAL_GPIO_PIN_RESET. An input without a pull that nothing drives reads an undefined level. Debouncing, thresholds and the external circuit are application matters; for an edge interrupt use gpio_input_interrupt instead. HAL/LL sources are already included and the declarations come from stm32_hal.h; do not redeclare them.
